chunks: What the Shaykh informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a woman who sees in sleep what a man sees. He said: “If she emits, then ghusl is obligatory upon her; and if she does not emit, then ghusl is not obligatory upon her.”

key_terms.أَنْزَلَتْ: she emitted fluid, which makes ghusl obligatory in this context
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman being asked about in the legal ruling
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: sleep or dream-state in which the experience occurs

ai.seo_question: Does a woman have to perform ghusl after seeing a sexual dream?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman who experiences a sexual dream. The obligation of ghusl depends on emission; if emission occurs, ghusl is required, and if it does not occur, ghusl is not required.
